sentences.text: Opposite Party :- State Of U.P Thru.Prin. Secy. Home Lko.

Counsel for Applicant :- Farooq Ayoob,Km. Pooja Tiwari Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Saurabh Lavania,J.
1.
Heard learned counsel for the applicant as well as learned A.G.A. for the State of U.P. and perused the record.

2. The present bail application has been filed on behalf of the applicant in Case Crime No.113 of 2024, under Sections 498A/304B IPC and 3/4 Dowry Prohibition Act, Police Station Ram Nagar,
District Barabanki, with the prayer to enlarge her on bail.
3. On query being asked, learned A.G.A. submitted that he has complete instructions in the matter as such this Court proceeded to hear the matter on merits.

4. It is submitted that the applicant aged about 55 years, has been implicated in the instant case by the informant (father of deceased) only on account of the fact that applicant is mother-in-law (Saas)

1 of the deceased.

5. It is also stated that the applicant has not committed any crime and the applicant having no criminal history, is in jail since 21.02.2024.
6.

It is further stated that marriage between the deceased and the son of the applicant namely Sandeep was solemnized on 07.05.2023 and the incident took place on 20.02.2024 and at the time of inquest two persons namely Suneel Yadav and Umesh, R/o Village Thalkhurd, Police Station Ram Nagar, District Barabanki, which is the place of residence of informant, were present and they are also the witnesses of inquest, which was carried out on 20.02.2024 and as per these witnesses, it is a case of suicide, however, while examining the body of deceased the Autopsy Surgeon could not ascertain the reason of death and accordingly the Viscera was preserved and sent for chemical examination, however, till date the report has not been placed before the trial court.

7. It is further submitted that a bare perusal of FIR, would indicate that against all accused persons vague and frivolous allegations have been levelled to attract the offence under Section 498A, 304B IPC and 3/4 Dowry Prohibition Act.
8. It is further submitted that practicing of implicating entire family members has been deprecated by the Hon'ble Apex Court.

In this regard reference has been made to the judgment passed by Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Geeta Mehrotra and others vs. State of U.P. and others reported in (2012) 10 SCC 741 and in the case of Kahkashan Kausar v. State of Bihar reported in (2022) 6 SCC 599.

sentences.text:
Lastly it is stated that the applicant being lady is also entitled to the benefit of Section 437 Cr.P.C.
9.
Learned Additional Government Advocate opposed the bail application however, she could not dispute the aforesaid facts.

10. Considering the aforesaid facts including the statements of witnesses of inquest, period of incarceration as also that chemical examination report is still awaited and the observations of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the judgment(s) referred above and the relationship of applicant and deceased and without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, I am of the view that applicant is entitled to be released on bail.
11. Let applicant- Pushpa Devi be released on bail in aforesaid Case Crime, on her furnishing personal bond to the satisfaction of the court concerned forthwith.

Applicant is also directed to furnish two reliable sureties each of the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned subject to following conditions:-
(i) The applicant shall cooperate with the prosecution during trial.
(ii) The applicant shall not tamper with the evidence during trial.

(iv) The applicant shall not commit an offence.

(v) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.

(vi) The applicant shall remain present before the trial court on each date fixed,
either personally or through counsel.
(vii) The applicant shall not seek any adjournment on the dates fixed for evidence when the witnesses are present in court.
(viii) The applicant shall remain present, in person, before the trial court on the dates fixed for recording of statement under Section 313 Cr.P.C.
